title: Jingnan
capsule: Jingnan (also called Nanping or Northern Chu) was the smallest and weakest of the Ten Kingdoms of China's Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period, a landlocked polity ruled by the Gao family from their capital at Jingzhou on the middle Yangzi. Founded by Gao Jixing in 924, the kingdom survived by playing the surrounding powers—Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han, Later Zhou, and the Song—against one another while collecting transit taxes on Yangzi commerce, earning a reputation for opportunistic tribute-seeking. All five Gao rulers held the title of prince rather than emperor and issued no era names, acknowledging formal suzerainty upward; in 963 the first Song emperor Taizu absorbed Jingnan without military resistance, completing the earliest step in his reunification of China.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Jingnan's territory around Jingzhou is well documented in Song-dynasty histories; the small kingdom's precise extent at any given year is reasonably mapped given the detailed Chinese administrative records.
